Patrick McPartland of Bowman is requesting a zoning determination for Project Aspen located at 20471 Goose Landing Lane, Leesburg - PIN: 194-49-8227. Specifically, that the proposed mechanical yard is located such that there are no adverse impacts on the adjacent properties.

2/21/2025
By way of background, the above referenced property (the “Property”) is split zoned 
Industrial Park (IP) and General Industry (GI) under the Loudoun County Zoning 
Ordinance. The IP portion of the Property is developed with existing data center use. 
The GI portion of the Property (“Project Aspen Site”) is the location of the Project 
Aspen data center that is subject to EPLAN-2024-0139 and this determination 
request. The Project Aspen Site is subject to Zoning Map Amendment (ZMAP)-2019-
0003 and Special Exception (SPEX)-2019-0003, Luck/Hayden/Loudoun Water 
Property approved February 18, 2020. EPLAN-2023-0128, Project Aspen, was 
approved November 15, 2024, for a single data center on the Project Aspen Site. 
EPLAN-2024-0139, Project Aspen, proposes a revision to approved EPLAN-2023-0128 to adjust the mechanical yard on the east side of the proposed Project Aspen data center building per new specifications provided by the Owner.

Staff notes EPLAN-2023-0128 was processed, reviewed, and approved under the land 
use and development regulations prescribed in the Revised 1993 Zoning Ordinance
pursuant to the Resolution of the Board of Supervisors of Loudoun County Virginia, 
Adopting Grandfathering Rules for ZOAM-2020-0001, Zoning Ordinance Rewrite 
(“Grandfathering Resolution”), adopted on December 13, 2023. EPLAN-2024-0138 is 
being processed and reviewed under the land use and development regulations 
prescribed in the Zoning Ordinance since EPLAN-2024-0138 was submitted after 
December 13, 2023 and is subject to the data center use specific standards in Zoning 
Ordinance Section 4.06.02. 

Table 4.06.02-2.b.1.d. of the Zoning Ordinance states the following:
No Screening Requirements Adjacent to Industrially Zoned Property.
As determined by the Zoning Administrator, Data Center Mechanical 
Equipment located in a manner found to have no adverse impact on adjacent 
properties zoned IP, GI, or MR-HI is not required to be screened pursuant to 
Section 4.06.02-2.b.1, except that Data Center Mechanical Equipment must 
be screened from any existing or planned public road.
Per the County’s geographic information system, WebLOGIS, the adjacent parcel 
information is as follows:
North: PIN: 152-25-4491, zoned MR-HI under the Zoning Ordinance. 
East: PIN: 152-26-8334, zoned GI under the Zoning Ordinance. 
South: PIN: 153-35-5865, zoned MR-HI under the Zoning Ordinance. 
West: PIN: 193-18-6982, zoned IP under the Zoning Ordinance. 
The adjacent parcel to the north, PIN: 152-25-4491, is currently vacant. The Project 
Aspen Site contains required buffer yard plantings as well as proffered reforestation 
area #1 along the northern property line. As such, Zoning Administration staff finds 
the mechanical equipment yard is located in a manner found to have no adverse 
impact on the adjacent parcel to the north zoned MR-HI.
The adjacent parcel to the east, PIN: 152-26-8334, is currently vacant. The Project 
Aspen Site contains a proffered Tree Conservation Area along the entirety of the 
eastern property line adjacent to PIN: 152-26-8334. As such, Zoning Administration 
staff finds the mechanical yard is located in a manner found to have no adverse 
impact on the adjacent parcel to the east zoned GI.
The adjacent parcel to the south, PIN: 153-35-5865, is currently improved with an 
existing Water Treatment Plant. Staff notes when EPLAN-2023-0128 was approved, 
a buffer yard was not required between the proposed Project Aspen data center 
(Group 10 buffer use group) and the existing Water Treatment Plant (Group 10 buffer 
use group). However, EPLAN-2023-0128 proposed to retain existing vegetation as 
Tree Conservation Area (Tree Conservation Area 3) along the southern property line 
adjacent to PIN: 153-35-5865. EPLAN-2024-0138 continues to depict Tree 
Conservation Area 3 along the southern property line adjacent to PIN: 153-35-5865. 
As such, Zoning Administration staff finds the mechanical yard is located in a manner 
found to have no adverse impact on the adjacent parcel to the south zoned MR-HI.
In regard to the visual impact on the Dulles Greenway, the southern property line of 
the Project Aspen Site adjacent to the Dulles Greenway contains a proffered Tree 
Conservation Area as depicted on Sheet 3A-C-9700 of EPLAN-2024-0139 and in lineof-sight elevation 03. Additionally, the Project Aspen Site contains proffered 
reforestation area #2 north of said proffered Tree Conservation Area. The Project 
Aspen data center building will also provide screening of the mechanical yard from 
the Dulles Greenway. As such, Zoning Administration staff finds the mechanical yard 
is sufficiently screened from the Dulles Greenway. 
The adjacent parcel to the west, PIN: 193-18-6982, has approved land development 
applications for data center development. Further, the existing data center use 
located on the IP portion of the Property is located between the Project Aspen Site 
and PIN: 193-18-6982. The Project Aspen mechanical yard is located behind the 
Project Aspen data center building to the east. As such, Zoning Administration staff 
finds the mechanical yard is located in a manner found to have no adverse impact on 
the adjacent property to the west zoned IP.

I am writing with regard to Loudoun County PIN 045-46-5016 (the “Property”), on behalf of 1501 Moran Road Development Owner LLC (the “Owner”), to request your office’s confirmation that the minor changes proposed with the currently in-process data center site plan amendment (EPLAN-2025-0149) for the Property are permitted pursuant to Section 10.11.01.H of the Loudoun County Zoning Ordinance (the “Zoning Ordinance”). As is detailed in Footnote #3 to Table 3.02.05-1 of the Zoning Ordinance, a site plan amendment application for minor changes to an approved site plan for a data center use (such approved site plan being EPLAN-2023-0087 in this case) is permitted without processing a Special Exception application, so long as the proposed changes are in conformance with Section 10.11.01.H of the Zoning Ordinance. 

More specifically, Section 10.11.01.H.2. of the Zoning Ordinance states, “the Zoning Administrator may permit minor changes to an approved Special Exception when such are reasonably necessary to address issues related to topography, drainage, underground utilities, structural safety, final engineering, vehicular circulation, or requirements of government agencies.” As confirmed by County Staff, under this scenario, EPLAN-2023-0087 (the “Approved Site Plan”) operates as the approved “Special Exception” for purposes of Section 10. Therefore, the Owner seeks the Zoning Administrator’s approval of the changes described herein to the Approved Site Plan to be processed as a site plan amendment, as minor changes necessitated by issues related to topography, final engineering, and vehicular circulation. 

As detailed within the plans submitted as part of EPLAN-2025-0149, the amendment proposes to slightly adjust the location of several improvements on the Property from what was originally shown on the Approved Site Plan, including the drive aisle and the building footprint. These changes are necessary following a final engineering analysis, which determined that the retaining wall shown on the Approved Site Plan is not constructible in its initially proposed location. As a result of moving the retaining wall, the originally contemplated location of the nearby drive aisle also requires a minor relocation. A slight shift to the proposed building footprint is in turn required to accommodate the relocation of the retaining wall and drive aisle. Notably, the amendment does not seek to change the size of the building footprint or the building’s square footage.

In all, these modifications are minor in nature and will result in a more efficient and achievable layout for the Property, which is still generally consistent with the intent of the Approved Site Plan. Given the foregoing, the owner of the Property respectfully requests your office’s determination that the modifications proposed with EPLAN-2025-0149 are consistent with Section 10.11.01.H of the Zoning Ordinance and that, accordingly, the site plan amendment can continue to process to final approval.

In accordance with Zoning Ordinance Section 10.11.01.H.2.b.2, prior to action on this request we will provide the Zoning Administrator with an affidavit that demonstrates that the required notice as set forth in Zoning Ordinance Section 10.11.01.H.2.b.1 has been sent.

Given EPLAN-2025-0149 is currently in-process, we would appreciate anything you can do to expediate the review and approval of this request. We will submit the County’s zoning determination request fee electronically.  Should you require any additional information, please don’t hesitate to call me at (703) 456-8572. Thank you in advance for your time.

Best,
Bria

Christie Grucella of Bohler Engineering is requesting a minor modification to SPEX for Brambleton Tech Park, EPLAN-2026-0053.

Pursuant to Table 3.02.05-1, Footnote #3, “Notwithstanding Section 1.02.E.2, a site plan or site plan amendment application for minor changes to an approved site plan for a data center use may be permitted without a SPEX approval. Such minor changes are subject to the provisions of Section 10.11.01.H, mutatis mutandis.” EPLAN-2026-0053, “Brambleton Tech Park” Site Plan Amendment was accepted for review on June 16, 2026, and is a site plan amendment for the proposed revisions discussed in your May 1, 2026, request letter. As depicted in EPLAN-2026-0053 and detailed in your request letter, the proposed site design changes consist of addition of switchgear equipment; installation of a retaining wall along the western property frontage; minor adjustments to the parking configuration adjacent to the two southern buildings; and changes to the cooling tanks at the end of the building, resulting in minor modifications to the associated drive aisle configuration and on-site circulation. These are the only changes to what was previously approved with STMP-2022-0018. Your letter indicates these changes are necessary to facilitate a functional and constructable site layout based on final engineering and vehicular circulation. 

Section 10.11.01.H.2. allows the Zoning Administrator to permit minor changes to an approved SPEX “when such are reasonably necessary to address issues related to topography, drainage, underground utilities, structural safety, final engineering, vehicular circulation, or requirements of government agencies.” Based on the site revisions described in your May 1, 2026, request letter and as depicted on EPLAN-2026-0053, staff find the site design changes are related to minor changes reasonably necessary to address issues related to final engineering and vehicular circulation. Therefore, the requested minor changes to STMP-2022-0018 are consistent with the provisions of Section 10.11.01.H.2. and are hereby granted as depicted in the exhibit provided with the May 1, 2026, request letter and in EPLAN-2026-0053.

ASHBURN EAST PH 2: This is an STMP application, and it is a revision to the previously approved STMP-2018-0006 and subsequent SPAM application SPAM-2019-0057 (Ashburn East Phase 1 & 2).  The previously approved plans proposed two data center buildings along with associated site utilities, travelways and parking areas on two parcels (PIN #s 061-030-1740 and 061-29-8643).  Stormwater Water Management (SWM) facilities serving the entire development on this parcel were also designed with original site plan. Building #1 (DC21), all the site travelways and most of the site utilities have been constructed and is shown on the Existing Conditions Sheet EX01.  All the previously SWM facilities have been installed except for the ones on the west and east side of proposed Building #2 (DC22).   The project is under active construction since 2019 is currently bonded with the County in two phases.  There is an active VSMP permit and grading permit for this site construction.
This Site Plan proposes revisions to Building #2 (DC22) located north of the site.  The site utilities, loading docks and some parking areas have been reconfigured for the revised building layout.   This plan has been submitted as a new STMP application because of the significant changes to the building footprint and gross floor area that precludes the submission as a SPAM.
